- When sentiment turns negative or shows strong downward momentum (e.g., sentiment change < -0.5), model tends to overcorrect or overshoot downward — reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overreacts with exaggerated downward correction — apply a “lagged mean reversion” rule: subtract 0.5–1.5% of the spike magnitude from forecast.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price declines (e.g., sentiment > 0.67 but price drops > 3%), model overestimates upside — cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.33), model often fails to capture mean reversion — use 3-day moving average of true price as baseline for correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) — apply a “first-day discount” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for day 1–5.
- If news volume is constant (3.0) and sentiment is volatile, model overfits to sentiment swings — dampen forecast by 0.3–0.7% per sentiment change > 0.33.
